name: Sri Venkateswara Temple
description: Ancient Vaishnavite temple atop the sacred Venkatadri hill of Seshachalam range, dedicated to Lord Venkateswara. Renowned for its Dravidian architectural heritage and historic gold-gilded Ananda Nilayam vimana.

name: Swami Pushkarini
description: Sacred water tank situated on the northern side of Sri Venkateswara Temple. Historically revered as a divine reservoir whose waters were consecrated by Garuda according to the Brahmanda Purana.

name: Sri Bedi Anjaneyaswami Temple
description: Historic shrine dedicated to Lord Hanuman, situated directly opposite the Mahadwaram of Sri Venkateswara Temple. Features antique Chola-Vijayanagara masonry and unique chained iconography.

name: Kapila Theertham
description: The sole ancient Shaivite pilgrimage site situated at the base of the Seshachalam hills in Tirupati, nestled beneath a natural mountain waterfall where sage Kapila Maharishi meditated.

name: Chandragiri Fort & Palaces
description: Prominent 11th-century fortification constructed by the Yadava Naidus, later serving as the fourth imperial capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. Preserves the Indo-Saracenic Raja Mahal and Rani Mahal.

name: Sri Govindaraja Swamy Temple
description: Vast Vaishnavite temple complex in the heart of Tirupati, consecrated by Saint Ramanujacharya in 1130 CE. Boasts an imposing seven-storey Raja Gopuram and intricate Vijayanagara mandapas.

name: Silathoranam (Natural Rock Arch)
description: Rare geological monument dating back to the Pre-Cambrian era (1500 million years ago), formed by weathering and erosion in the Cuddapah Supergroup quartzites atop Tirumala hills.

name: Sri Varahaswami Temple
description: Ancient temple on the banks of Swami Pushkarini, dedicated to Adi Varaha. According to centuries-old temple tradition and inscriptions, pilgrims visit Varahaswami before the main sanctum.
